Jim Ginty and Pat Parker were in the leading bunch, and Dan Patience and Bert Footer were close behind. The second lap showed us to have a twenty to thirty points lead over our Midland rivals but on the next lap they managed to reduce our lead slightly....

In the Spring of 1937, Bill was brought in as a reserve for an Olympic runner, Jim Ginty in the London - Brighton Relay and ran a splendid sixth stage to maintain the lead we then held, and which was only lost in the last few yards at Brighton.

At 1 mile Birchfield led; at 2 miles we were leading handsomely, but in the last lap our Midland friends managed to pack in together and inflict a 4 points defeat upon us." Jim Ginty won the event with a time of 14 mins 43 secs.
